subject: Post-demo: Itemized privacy points — residency, logs, DPA mapping
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nsharma@redwood.com>
To: Emma Lo <emma.lo@medcorp.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: Itemized privacy points — residency, logs, DPA mapping

Emma / Chris —

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap and a short list of items we agreed to follow up on so your legal and infra teams can evaluate: 

1) Residency: You flagged a requirement that all production inference for the pilot must remain in the US (multi-region unacceptable). Can you confirm whether a single us-west region is acceptable or if you need specific state-level residency?

2) PII scope: You said protected health identifiers (PHI) will be redacted prior to ingestion for the first phase; however you also asked whether Redwood retains request/response payloads for 30 days for debugging. Our default is 30 days for logging unless configured otherwise — we can reduce retention or enable strict access controls. Please confirm the required retention period and whether logs must be disabled entirely.

3) Access & audit logs: You requested per-token request tracing and immutable audit logs exportable to your SIEM. We can provide token-level latency/cost breakdowns and per-request trace IDs; exports can be pushed to S3 or a customer-managed logging endpoint. What format and frequency do you prefer?

4) Subprocessors & breach notification: You asked about subprocessor notifications and DPA breach timelines. Our standard DPA requires us to notify controller customers within 48 hours after confirming a breach that affects customer data; we can discuss pushing that to 24 hours in the contract for enterprise. For subprocessors, we provide an updated list quarterly and notify customers for any material changes.

5) Next steps: Attached is a redline of our standard DPA (DPA_Redline_v1.pdf) and a basic data map spreadsheet (MedCorp_Data_Map.xlsx) — please share these with legal/infosec. Can you confirm who on your side will own the written responses (legal or infra)? Also propose times for a second follow-up if we need to get legal on the call.

Thanks — short items so your team can triage. Happy to sync with Monica or Ben for any technical walkthroughs.

—
Nikhil Sharma
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Lo <emma.lo@medcorp.com>

Cc: Chris Dunn <chris.dunn@healthsync.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-09-01T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Itemized privacy points — residency, logs, DPA mapping

Thanks Nikhil — useful summary. A few clarifications from legal/infra here: 

- Residency: us-west (Oregon) is fine for the pilot; long-term we will evaluate multi-AZ within the same state. No cross-border replication allowed.

- Retention: We cannot keep unredacted request/response payloads for more than 7 days. Debug logs with PII must be turned off unless on-demand for incident triage and then purged immediately after. Audit logs that only contain request metadata (no payload) may be retained for 90 days.

- Access logs format: We prefer JSON lines with a request_id, model, timestamp, region, and per-token cost estimates. Daily delivery to an S3 bucket with server-side encryption is preferred.

- Breach notify: Our legal prefers a 24-hour initial notification for incidents that materially affect our customer data. Also need to understand the playbook for subprocessor notifications — specifically, do you notify customers only after confirming impact, or upon discovery of a subprocessor event?

I'll share these notes with our counsel. My in-house legal contact is Chris Dunn (cc'd); he will confirm the 24-hour ask.

—Emma
Emma Lo
Head of Integrations, MedCorp Health
emma.lo@medcorp.com

Emma — thanks for the clarifications. Couple of concrete action items from our side: 

- We will prepare a S3 export manifest template that matches your JSON-lines schema (request_id, model, timestamp, region, token_cost). Expect to see that in your Drive by EOD today: https://drive.redwood.com/medcorp/privacy-playbook

- Regarding retention: Engineering confirms we can implement a 7-day purge for unredacted payloads plus a configurable "on-demand triage" toggle that temporarily retains redacted payloads for 48 hours when enabled by a customer admin. We'll document the admin flow and retention logs for audit.

- Breach + subprocessor communications: Legal can provide a revised DPA clause that commits to a 24-hour initial notification window and a definition for "material impact." I can set up a brief (30-min) call next week with our legal lead to walk through proposed wording — does Wednesday 9/8 11:00am PT work for you? If so, we'll have Ben join for the contract/redline walkthrough.

- I've uploaded a lightly annotated DPA redline and a starter data flow diagram in the Drive folder — take a look and tell us any gaps.

- MedCorp legal confirms 24-hour ask (Chris)
